intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

selected_hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Embark on a full-day speedboat tour hopping between the stunning Phi Phi islands, including Maya Bay, Monkey Beach, and Pileh Lagoon. Snorkel in crystal-clear turquoise waters teeming with colorful marine life and explore dramatic limestone cliffs rising from the Andaman Sea.

experiences.name: Bangkok Street Food Night Market Tour
experiences.description: Dive deep into Bangkok's legendary street food scene with a guided evening walk through Yaowarat (Chinatown) and Silom. Sample iconic dishes like pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, boat noodles, and fresh papaya salad from legendary local vendors and hawker stalls.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Sunset Beach Kayaking
experiences.description: Paddle a sea kayak along the serene mangrove coastline and hidden sea caves of Koh Lanta during golden hour. Explore secluded coves inaccessible by boat, spot wildlife in the mangroves, and finish with a breathtaking sunset over the Andaman Sea from a quiet stretch of white sand beach.

experiences.name: Chiang Mai Street Food & Night Bazaar Experience
experiences.description: Wander through Chiang Mai's famous Sunday Walking Street and Night Bazaar, sampling northern Thai specialties like khao soi (coconut curry noodles), sai oua (herb sausage), and crispy pork rinds. Engage with local vendors, browse handmade crafts, and soak in the vibrant cultural atmosphere of the old city.
experiences.location: Wualai Road & Night Bazaar, Chiang Mai

experiences.name: Similan Islands Full-Day Snorkeling Expedition
experiences.description: Join a full-day boat excursion to the world-renowned Similan Islands National Park, consistently ranked among the top snorkeling and diving destinations globally. Swim alongside whale sharks, manta rays, and vibrant coral gardens at multiple pristine sites, and relax on powdery white sand beaches between dives.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi or Phuket Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, exchange currency at the airport (avoid airport exchange booths — use ATMs for better rates). Take a budget minivan or shared taxi to the pier. Catch a ferry to Phi Phi Islands (Rassada Pier in Phuket or Ao Nang in Krabi). Settle into your boutique stay, freshen up, and explore the immediate surroundings of Tonsai Village.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Tonsai Bay beachfront. Grab dinner at one of the local open-air restaurants on the walking street. Watch the famous Phi Phi sunset from the pier area.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or during transit — grab a simple Thai rice porridge (khao tom) or a convenience store snack from 7-Eleven (under 60 THB)
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a quick pad thai or spring rolls from a street stall near the pier while waiting for the ferry (80–120 THB)
meals.dinner: Tonsai Village Walking Street — try a local restaurant for pad kra pao (basil stir-fry) with rice and a Chang beer (150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry from Phuket to Phi Phi costs around 200–350 THB one way. Book in advance during high season. October may bring some rain — pack a light rain jacket. Keep 500 THB cash handy for ferry and transport tips.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike to the Phi Phi Viewpoint (30–45 min uphill trek). The panoramic view of both Tonsai and Loh Dalum bays is breathtaking and absolutely free. Bring water and wear good shoes. Return to the hotel for a quick freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Loh Dalum Bay — a gorgeous crescent-shaped bay on the north side of Phi Phi Don. Swim, snorkel along the rocks, and relax on the beach. Rent a snorkel set from a local shop (80–100 THB/hour). Explore the colorful coral near the bay's edges.
day_by_day.evening: Join the lively Tonsai Village night scene. Browse the night market stalls for souvenirs and street food. Watch fire show performances on the beach (free to watch, tip the performers if you enjoy it).

meals.breakfast: Mama's Restaurant near Tonsai — local Thai breakfast with coffee, eggs, and toast (100–150 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside vendor at Loh Dalum — fresh fruit skewers, mango sticky rice, and coconut water (100 THB total)
meals.dinner: Night market on the walking street — mix and match dishes: som tum (papaya salad), grilled skewers, and fried rice (150–180 THB)

day_by_day.notes: The viewpoint hike is best done before 9:00 AM to avoid heat. Entrance fee to the viewpoint is around 30 THB. Loh Dalum Bay is a 10-minute walk from Tonsai. October weather may be overcast — check forecasts daily.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget snorkeling longtail boat tour departing from Tonsai Pier. Visit Maya Bay (famous from 'The Beach'), Pileh Lagoon, and Monkey Beach. Longtail boat charters can be split with other travelers — negotiate for 400–600 THB per person for a half-day tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the boat tour by early afternoon. Rest at the hotel or relax on Tonsai Beach. Alternatively, rent a kayak (150–200 THB/hour) and paddle around the coastline independently.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the quieter side streets of Tonsai Village. Visit a local 7-Eleven or Family Mart for snacks and drinks. Enjoy a quiet evening on the beach watching the stars.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or a nearby bakery — banana pancake and fresh juice (80–120 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the boat tour — buy from 7-Eleven the night before (60–80 THB). Or eat at a beachside shack near Maya Bay pier area.
meals.dinner: Local Thai restaurant in Tonsai — massaman curry with rice and a fresh lime soda (180–220 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has restricted access and timed entry — confirm with your boat operator the current rules. Book longtail boat tours the evening before for better prices. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a dry bag for electronics.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning ferry from Phi Phi Don to Phi Phi Leh (or arrange a separate longtail). Explore Viking Cave — an ancient cave with prehistoric cave paintings and bird's nest collection scaffolding. Then visit the tranquil Loh Samah Bay for swimming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phi Phi Don by midday. Spend the afternoon at the less-crowded Long Beach (Hat Yao) on the southeast side of the island — a 15-minute longtail ride or 30-minute walk from Tonsai. Snorkel among sea turtles often spotted here.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Tonsai by longtail water taxi (50 THB). Enjoy a relaxed evening with a beachside drink at sunset. Try one of the budget beach bars for a happy hour cocktail.

meals.breakfast: Street stall near the pier — khao man gai (chicken rice) or jok (rice porridge) (60–90 THB)
meals.lunch: Longtail boat snacks or a small restaurant at Long Beach — grilled fish with rice (150–180 THB)
meals.dinner: Tonsai Village — tom yum soup and fried rice combo at a local restaurant (160–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Long Beach is quieter and less touristy — a great escape from the Tonsai crowds. Water taxis between Tonsai and Long Beach run frequently. October can bring afternoon rain showers — plan outdoor activities for morning hours.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry from Phi Phi Islands to Krabi Town (approximately 1.5–2 hours, 250–350 THB). Check into a budget guesthouse in Krabi Town near Chao Fah Park. Explore the quirky Krabi Town Walking Street area and the famous giant crab statues by the river.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Wat Kaew Korawaram — a beautiful white Buddhist temple in the center of Krabi Town, free to enter. Walk through the local fresh market near the pier. Take a short longtail boat ride along the Krabi River to see mangroves (negotiate 200–300 THB for a 1-hour ride).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Krabi Town Night Market (open evenings) near Maharaj Road for incredible street food variety and local handicrafts.

meals.breakfast: Quick bite at Phi Phi pier before departure — roti with banana and condensed milk (50–70 THB)
meals.lunch: Krabi Town fresh market — local noodle soup, grilled pork skewers, and fresh coconut (100–130 THB)
meals.dinner: Krabi Night Market — pad see ew, mango sticky rice, and grilled seafood skewers (150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets from Phi Phi to Krabi at least one day in advance. Krabi Town is a great base for exploring Railay Beach and the surrounding islands. Budget guesthouses in Krabi Town range from 300–600 THB/night.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Krabi Town or Ao Nang to Railay Beach (only accessible by boat, 100–150 THB each way). Explore Railay East and West beaches. Hike to the Railay Viewpoint for stunning karst limestone views — a challenging but rewarding 45-minute scramble.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Phra Nang Cave Beach — one of Thailand's most photographed beaches with a sacred cave shrine. Snorkel in the crystal-clear waters. Explore the Diamond Cave (Tham Phra Nang Nok) nearby — free entry, bring a flashlight.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town by longtail before dark. Relax at a riverside café and enjoy the slower pace of Krabi Town compared to the islands.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or street vendor near the pier — fried egg on rice with chili sauce (60–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Railay Beach restaurant — shared plates of spring rolls, papaya salad, and fried rice (200–250 THB for two)
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant in Krabi Town — fresh seafood soup and steamed jasmine rice (180–220 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach can only be reached by longtail boat — last boats return around 18:00–19:00. Phra Nang Cave contains a fertility shrine — be respectful. Wear good grip shoes for the viewpoint hike as it involves rope climbing.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget 4-island tour departing from Krabi Town or Ao Nang pier. Typical stops include Koh Poda, Chicken Island (Koh Kai), Koh Tup, and Koh Mor — famous for the sandbar that connects islands at low tide. Tour costs 500–700 THB including snorkeling gear and lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island hopping tour. Snorkel at Koh Poda's coral reef. Take photos at the iconic Chicken Island rock formation. Return to Krabi Town by 16:00.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Chao Fah Night Bazaar for dinner and shopping. Buy local spices, dried fruits, and Thai snacks as souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Street stall near Ao Nang — khao niao mamuang (mango sticky rice) and Thai iced coffee (80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Included in the 4-island tour package — typically a simple Thai meal on one of the islands
meals.dinner: Chao Fah Night Bazaar — grilled corn, pad thai, satay skewers, and fresh fruit shake (150–180 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Book the 4-island tour through your guesthouse or a local travel agent for the best price — avoid booking through large hotel lobbies. The sandbar between islands is only visible at low tide — check tide schedules. Bring cash for the tour.

day_by_day.morning: Take a minivan or local bus from Krabi to Ao Nang (30–40 minutes, 50–80 THB). Explore Ao Nang Beach — a lively resort town with great beach access. Walk the main strip and compare prices for activities. Rent a beach chair and umbrella (100 THB) and relax.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a longtail boat to Shell Cemetery (Susan Hoi) — a unique geological site with 75-million-year-old fossilized shells forming a rocky beach. Entry is free. Then visit the nearby Ao Nang Elephant Sanctuary for an ethical elephant encounter (book ahead, 1,500–2,000 THB — a splurge worth budgeting for).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Ao Nang beachfront strip at night — buzzing with restaurants, bars, and street food stalls. Great people-watching spot.

meals.breakfast: Ao Nang street vendor — banana roti with Nutella and a Thai iced tea (70–90 THB)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant away from the beachfront (cheaper prices) — green curry with rice and water (130–160 THB)
meals.dinner: Ao Nang beachfront — grilled prawns, som tum, and sticky rice with a local beer (200–250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Ao Nang is more expensive than Krabi Town — eat at restaurants one street back from the beach for better value. The elephant sanctuary requires advance booking. Shell Cemetery is a short longtail ride from Ao Nang pier (negotiate 200–300 THB round trip).

day_by_day.morning: Take a bus or minivan from Krabi to Koh Lanta (approximately 2–3 hours including ferry crossing, 250–350 THB). Check into a budget bungalow on Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao). Koh Lanta is quieter and more laid-back than Phi Phi — perfect for a slower pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Long Beach — a 4 km stretch of golden sand with calm waters ideal for swimming. Rent a scooter (200–250 THB/day) to explore the island independently. Drive south to the quieter Klong Nin Beach for a peaceful afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the west coast of Koh Lanta — one of the best sunset views in Krabi Province. Dine at a beachside restaurant on Long Beach.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure in Krabi — street stall rice and egg (60 THB) or guesthouse breakfast
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant on Koh Lanta — local Thai lunch set with soup, main, and rice (100–130 THB)
meals.dinner: Long Beach beachside restaurant — fresh catch of the day grilled with garlic and herbs, served with rice (200–250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta has a more relaxed vibe — great for travelers seeking quieter beaches. Scooter rental is the most efficient way to explore the island. October is shoulder/low season on Koh Lanta — some businesses may be closed but prices are lower.

day_by_day.morning: Ride your scooter to Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Si Raya) on the east coast — a charming historic Chinese-Malay fishing village with wooden shophouses built on stilts over the sea. Explore the small streets, local cafes, and handicraft shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Mu Ko Lanta National Park at the southern tip of the island (entrance fee 200 THB). Walk to the lighthouse for panoramic views. Snorkel at the park's beach. Then drive to Bamboo Bay (Ao Mai Phai) — a hidden gem accessible by scooter with excellent snorkeling.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Long Beach for a sunset swim. Enjoy a laid-back evening at one of the beachside bars with cushion seating on the sand.

meals.breakfast: Koh Lanta Old Town café — traditional Malay-style breakfast with roti canai and teh tarik (milk tea) (80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: National Park area — packed lunch from a local shop or simple restaurant near the park entrance (100–130 THB)
meals.dinner: Long Beach — BBQ seafood platter at a local beach restaurant, shared with fellow travelers (200–280 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta Old Town is a UNESCO-listed heritage area — be respectful of the community. The national park road is winding — drive carefully on the scooter. Bamboo Bay is best visited at low tide for the best snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget snorkeling trip from Koh Lanta to the surrounding islands — Koh Rok, Koh Ha, or Koh Ngai (prices vary 700–1,200 THB depending on destination). These islands have some of the best coral reefs in the Andaman Sea. Book through your guesthouse the evening before.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island snorkeling tour. Koh Rok is famous for its shallow turquoise lagoon and vibrant coral gardens. Enjoy a packed lunch on the beach of one of the uninhabited islands.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta by late afternoon. Pack bags and prepare for departure the next morning. Enjoy a final relaxed dinner on Long Beach.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or street stall — fried rice with egg (80 THB) before the early boat departure
meals.lunch: Included in the island snorkeling tour package — simple Thai meal on the island
meals.dinner: Long Beach farewell dinner — pad thai, tom kha soup, and fresh watermelon juice (180–220 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok requires a national park entry fee (200 THB) on top of the tour cost. Some tour operators include this in the price — confirm when booking. This is one of the most beautiful snorkeling experiences in southern Thailand — highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry or minivan from Koh Lanta back to Krabi Town (2–3 hours, 250–350 THB). From Krabi, take a bus or minivan to Ao Nang or directly to Phuket (2–2.5 hours, 150–250 THB). Check into a budget guesthouse in Phuket Old Town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Phuket Old Town — a beautifully preserved Sino-Portuguese heritage district with colorful shophouses, street art, and temples. Walk Thalang Road and Soi Romanee — the most photogenic streets. Visit Wat Mongkol Nimit temple (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Visit the famous Phuket Sunday Walking Street (if it's Sunday) or the Phuket Weekend Night Market (Naka Market) for incredible street food and local goods. If neither is on, explore the Old Town night food scene on Thalang Road.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure from Koh Lanta — simple noodle soup from a local stall (60–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Phuket Old Town local restaurant — khao mok gai (Thai chicken biryani) or local Hokkien noodles (100–130 THB)
meals.dinner: Phuket Walking Street / Night Market — dim sum, oyster omelette, satay, and fresh tropical fruit (150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Old Town is very walkable — wear comfortable shoes. The Sino-Portuguese architecture is best photographed in the late afternoon golden hour. Budget guesthouses in Phuket Old Town range from 350–700 THB/night and are far better value than Patong Beach area.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Phuket — visit the Big Buddha (Phra Phutta Ming Mongkol Akenakiri) on Nakkerd Hill. Entry is free. The 45-meter white marble statue offers panoramic views of Phuket and the Andaman Sea. Dress modestly (sarongs available to borrow at the entrance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Patong or Kata Beach for one last swim in the Andaman Sea. Browse Patong's Bangla Road area by day (much calmer than at night). Pick up last-minute souvenirs from local markets — elephant pants, Thai spices, and handmade crafts. Head to Phuket International Airport with plenty of time.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phuket International Airport. Grab a final Thai meal at the airport — look for local food courts rather than international chains for better value (150–200 THB).

meals.breakfast: Phuket Old Town — local coffee shop breakfast with kaya toast, soft-boiled eggs, and kopi (traditional coffee) (80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside vendor at Kata or Patong — fresh coconut, grilled corn, and pad thai (120–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Airport food court — final bowl of tom yum noodles or green curry with rice (150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Phuket Airport. The Big Buddha is a 20–30 minute drive from Old Town — take a local tuk-tuk or Grab (ride-hailing app) for 200–300 THB. Use remaining Thai baht at the airport or exchange back before departure.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, collect luggage and take a pre-booked ferry or speedboat transfer from Krabi or Phuket pier to Phi Phi Islands (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Check in to your boutique hotel, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along Tonsai Bay to get oriented with the island.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Tonsai Village walking street. Browse local shops, watch fire shows on the beach, and soak in the vibrant Phi Phi nightlife atmosphere at a relaxed pace.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or meal at the airport before departure.
meals.lunch: Quick bite at the pier café or convenience snack during the ferry journey.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Papaya Restaurant in Tonsai Village — affordable Thai classics like pad thai, green curry, and fresh seafood at mid-range prices (approx. 200–350 THB per dish).

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry transfer in advance to avoid delays. Arrive at Krabi or Phuket pier with enough buffer time. October can bring some rain showers — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise hike up to Phi Phi Viewpoint (30–45 minute climb). The panoramic view over both bays of Koh Phi Phi Don is spectacular and well worth the effort. Bring water and wear good shoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day snorkeling longtail boat tour around Phi Phi's nearby reefs — visit Monkey Beach, Loh Samah Bay, and the famous Viking Cave. Swim with colorful fish in crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on Loh Dalum Beach as the sun sets. Enjoy a beachfront drink at one of the casual beach bars before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or grab fresh fruit, roti, and coffee from a Tonsai Village street stall (approx. 80–120 THB).
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachside shack near Monkey Beach or pack snacks for the boat tour.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant — a beloved Phi Phi institution known for excellent Thai and international dishes at mid-range prices.

day_by_day.notes: Book the snorkeling longtail tour the evening before or through your hotel. Wear reef-safe sunscreen. The viewpoint hike is best done before 8:00 AM to avoid heat and crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day island hopping tour to the Phi Phi Leh islands — depart by speedboat to Maya Bay (the famous 'The Beach' filming location), Pileh Lagoon, and Loh Samah Bay. Swim, snorkel, and photograph stunning limestone karsts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island hopping tour to Bamboo Island (Koh Phai) — relax on the white sand beach, swim in turquoise waters, and enjoy a packed lunch on board or on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don by late afternoon. Shower and unwind before heading out for a casual evening walk through the village market.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the tour departs (usually 7:30–8:00 AM).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch included in most island hopping tour packages, typically Thai rice boxes and fresh fruit.
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at Tonsai Night Market — try mango sticky rice, grilled satay skewers, pad see ew, and fresh spring rolls (budget approx. 150–250 THB total).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Maya Bay speedboat tour at least a day ahead — it is very popular. Maya Bay has timed entry restrictions to protect the ecosystem; your tour operator will handle permits. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning kayaking session around the quieter eastern coast of Koh Phi Phi Don. Paddle through hidden coves, sea caves, and mangrove channels. Rentals available near Tonsai Pier (approx. 200–400 THB/hour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxed afternoon at Long Beach (Hat Yao) — one of Phi Phi's best beaches for swimming. Take a 10-minute longtail boat ride from Tonsai Pier. Lounge on the beach, swim, and read.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a cliff-side bar overlooking Loh Dalum Bay. Watch the famous Phi Phi fire show performances on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café — try khao tom (Thai rice soup) or toast with eggs and fresh juice (approx. 100–150 THB).
meals.lunch: Casual beachside lunch at Long Beach — grilled fish, som tum (papaya salad), and fresh coconut (approx. 200–300 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cosmic Restaurant on Phi Phi — known for good Thai food, wood-fired pizza, and a lively atmosphere at mid-range prices.

day_by_day.notes: Long Beach is calm and less crowded than Loh Dalum — ideal for a relaxed swim. October seas can occasionally be choppy; confirm longtail boat availability with locals.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Phi Phi boutique hotel. Take the morning ferry to Krabi Town (approximately 1.5 hours). Arrive and check in to a mid-range guesthouse or boutique hotel in Krabi Town or Ao Nang area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Krabi Town's charming riverside promenade along the Krabi River. Visit the famous frog statues, browse local markets, and visit Wat Kaew Korawaram temple for beautiful murals and a hilltop Buddha statue.
day_by_day.evening: Walk through Krabi's vibrant Night Walking Street (open Thursday–Sunday) or the weekend market for street food, local crafts, and live music.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Tonsai Village before ferry departure — roti with banana and condensed milk is a local favorite.
meals.lunch: Lunch at May and Mark's Kitchen in Krabi Town — a beloved local spot for authentic southern Thai cuisine at very reasonable prices (approx. 80–150 THB per dish).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Krabi Night Market or Chao Fa Night Market — sample fresh grilled seafood, noodle soups, and Thai desserts (budget approx. 150–200 THB).

day_by_day.notes: Book your Krabi accommodation in advance. The ferry schedule from Phi Phi to Krabi typically runs at 9:00 AM and 11:00 AM — confirm the day before. Store luggage at the pier if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the iconic Railay Beach — accessible only by longtail boat from Ao Nang (15-minute ride, approx. 100 THB each way). Explore Railay West Beach and Phra Nang Cave Beach, known for dramatic limestone cliffs and emerald water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the jungle trail from Railay East to the Railay Viewpoint for sweeping views over the peninsula. Then relax at Phra Nang Beach — consistently rated one of Thailand's most beautiful beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return by longtail to Ao Nang for sunset. Stroll along the Ao Nang beachfront promenade and browse the lively strip of restaurants and shops.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Krabi hotel or a café near the Ao Nang pier.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Railay Beach — fresh seafood or Thai dishes at one of the casual restaurants (approx. 200–350 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Last Fisherman Bar in Ao Nang — great seafood, Thai dishes, and cocktails with a relaxed beachfront vibe.

day_by_day.notes: Longtail boats to Railay depart from Ao Nang Beach — arrange a tuk-tuk or songthaew from Krabi Town to Ao Nang (approx. 60–100 THB). Wear water shoes as you may need to wade ashore.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for panoramic views over Krabi's landscape. Start early to avoid the midday heat. Entry is free; modest dress required.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Krabi Hot Springs and Emerald Pool (Sa Morakot) in Khao Phanom Bencha National Park. Soak in natural warm pools and swim in the stunning turquoise Emerald Pool surrounded by jungle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town for a relaxed evening. Visit a traditional Thai massage parlor for a 1-hour massage (approx. 250–350 THB) before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast near Tiger Cave Temple — local stalls sell congee, fried eggs, and Thai iced coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near the Emerald Pool — pack snacks and drinks, or eat at the small food stalls at the park entrance.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ruean Mai Restaurant in Krabi Town — excellent authentic Thai food in a traditional wooden house setting at mid-range prices.

day_by_day.notes: Hire a local driver or join a shared minivan tour to visit the Hot Springs and Emerald Pool (approx. 500–700 THB including transport and entry). The Tiger Cave climb is strenuous — bring plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early ferry or speedboat from Krabi to Koh Lanta (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Check in to a mid-range beachfront resort on Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) — Koh Lanta's most popular and family-friendly beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter or bicycle and explore Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Si Raya) — a charming stilted fishing village with Sino-Portuguese shophouses, local cafés, and artisan shops along the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the western coast of Koh Lanta — the sunsets here are among the best in southern Thailand. Enjoy drinks at a beachfront bar as the sky turns orange and pink.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the ferry or at a café near the Krabi pier before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Koh Lanta Old Town — try fresh grilled fish with rice and som tum (approx. 150–250 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mango House Restaurant in Koh Lanta Old Town — beautiful setting in a heritage building with excellent Thai and seafood dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Ferries to Koh Lanta from Krabi typically run October through April — confirm schedule as October is shoulder season. Scooter rental on Koh Lanta costs approx. 200–300 THB/day; bring your license.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling and island hopping day trip from Koh Lanta to the Koh Rok islands — pristine twin islands with some of the clearest water and best coral reefs in Thailand. Depart by speedboat (approx. 1.5 hours each way).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkeling at Koh Haa (Five Islands) — a protected marine park with incredible underwater visibility, sea turtles, and diverse marine life. Swim, relax on the boat, and enjoy the remote beauty.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta by late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy a beachside dinner as the stars appear over the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your resort before the tour departs (usually 7:30–8:00 AM).
meals.lunch: Lunch included in the Koh Rok day trip package — typically Thai rice boxes and fresh fruit served on the boat or beach.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Drunken Sailors Restaurant on Long Beach — popular spot with great Thai food, fresh seafood, and a lively but relaxed atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Koh Rok and Koh Haa snorkeling tour through your hotel or a local operator (approx. 1,200–1,800 THB per person). October may have some wind — check sea conditions. These islands are only accessible by boat tour.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Koh Lanta's interior — visit Khao Mai Kaew Cave for a guided spelunking adventure through stalactite-filled chambers (approx. 200 THB with a local guide). Then visit the Koh Lanta Animal Welfare elephant sanctuary for an ethical elephant experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a relaxed afternoon at Klong Nin Beach — a quieter, more laid-back stretch of sand with a bohemian vibe, calm waters, and excellent beachside cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Koh Lanta's famous sunset strip along the western coast. Watch the sun dip below the horizon from a swing or hammock at one of the beachfront bars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your resort or a local café on Long Beach.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside café on Klong Nin Beach — try fresh seafood, green papaya salad, and fresh coconut water.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Time for Lime Cooking School Restaurant — dine on dishes prepared by students; excellent quality Thai food at mid-range prices with a great social atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: The elephant sanctuary visit should be booked in advance. Verify it is a genuine ethical sanctuary (no riding). Scooter rental makes exploring Koh Lanta's beaches and interior much easier.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Koh Lanta accommodation. Take the ferry back to Krabi and then onward to Phuket by bus or shared minivan (total journey approx. 3–4 hours). Check in to a mid-range hotel in Phuket Old Town or Patong area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Phuket Old Town on foot — admire the colorful Sino-Portuguese shophouses along Thalang Road and Soi Romanee, visit the Blue Elephant Mansion, and browse independent boutiques and art galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Phuket Old Town's vibrant evening scene. Visit the Sunday Walking Street market (if it's Sunday) or explore the lively Lard Yai Night Market for street food and local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Koh Lanta hotel before checkout.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant in Phuket Old Town upon arrival — try Kopitiam by Wilai for authentic Phuket-style cuisine and local specialties like mee hokkien.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Phuket Old Town Night Market or a local restaurant — try oh tao (oyster pancake), moo hong (braised pork), and roti with curry.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Phuket accommodation in advance. The transfer from Koh Lanta to Phuket involves a ferry plus a minivan or bus — book through a travel agent or your hotel for a seamless connection.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Phang Nga Bay — join a longtail boat or kayaking tour through the dramatic limestone karsts, sea caves, and mangroves of one of Thailand's most iconic natural landscapes. Visit James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Phang Nga Bay tour with kayaking through hongs (hidden lagoons accessible only at certain tides) — a magical and serene experience. Visit a floating Muslim fishing village.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phuket by late afternoon. Enjoy a final evening in Phuket — visit Patong Beach for a lively atmosphere or stay in Old Town for a quieter, more cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your hotel before the Phang Nga Bay tour departs.
meals.lunch: Lunch included in most Phang Nga Bay tour packages — seafood lunch at a local restaurant near the bay.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Suay Restaurant in Phuket Old Town — creative Thai cuisine with local ingredients in a stylish heritage setting at mid-range prices.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Phang Nga Bay tour (approx. 1,200–1,800 THB) through your hotel or a reputable operator. Tours typically depart at 8:00 AM. Choose a kayaking-focused tour for the most immersive experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Phuket — visit Wat Chalong, Phuket's most important and ornate Buddhist temple. Light incense, explore the grand pagoda, and reflect on the journey. Then head to the Big Buddha statue on Nakkerd Hill for sweeping island views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Phuket Weekend Market (Naka Market) or Central Festival Phuket mall. Pick up Thai spices, silk scarves, local snacks, and handicrafts as gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Phuket International Airport for your departure flight. Arrive at least 2–3 hours before your flight. Enjoy a final Thai meal at the airport.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at a café in Phuket Old Town — try kaya toast, soft-boiled eggs, and Thai iced tea for a classic local morning.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Big Buddha or a final bowl of khao man gai (Hainanese chicken rice) from a local stall (approx. 60–100 THB).
meals.dinner: Final meal at the airport or a quick street food stop before departure — pad thai, mango sticky rice, or a fresh smoothie to end the trip on a high note.

day_by_day.notes: Allow 45–60 minutes to travel from Phuket Old Town to the airport depending on traffic. Keep some Thai baht for last-minute purchases and tips. Check airline baggage allowance if you have purchased extra items during the trip.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Clear customs and collect luggage at the airport, then arrange a premium private transfer to Krabi or Ao Nang Pier. Board a pre-arranged private longtail boat or speedboat transfer to your boutique stay on Phi Phi Islands. Enjoy the stunning Andaman Sea scenery en route. Check in, settle into your luxury villa or suite, and enjoy a welcome drink while taking in the views of the turquoise bay.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Tonsai Village's vibrant walking street to soak in the island atmosphere. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at a clifftop or beachfront restaurant such as the Phi Phi Natural Resort restaurant or Unni's Restaurant, known for fresh seafood and Thai classics with panoramic views.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Light snack or meal at the airport or onboard transfer
meals.dinner: Beachfront fine dining at a top-rated Phi Phi restaurant — grilled tiger prawns, green curry, and fresh coconut for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your speedboat or private longtail transfer in advance to avoid delays. October is shoulder season — expect warm weather with occasional brief rain showers. Pack a light rain jacket in your carry-on.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise yoga session on the beach arranged through your boutique stay. Follow with a premium Thai breakfast at the hotel — fresh tropical fruits, congee, and Thai-style eggs. Then embark on a private guided snorkeling excursion around Phi Phi's famous Hin Klang and Bida Nok reef systems, renowned for crystal-clear waters and vibrant coral life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Maya Bay on Phi Phi Leh — access is now managed with timed entry to protect the ecosystem. Swim in the emerald lagoon and explore the dramatic limestone cliffs. Continue to Pileh Lagoon for a private swim in its enclosed turquoise waters. Return to the hotel for a spa treatment — opt for a traditional Thai massage or aromatherapy session at the boutique stay's wellness facility.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Phi Phi Viewpoint for a golden-hour sunset hike — a 20-minute climb rewards with breathtaking panoramic views of both bays. Descend and enjoy dinner at a premium beachside restaurant featuring a curated seafood platter and craft cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — tropical fruit platter, Thai-style omelets, fresh juices, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch prepared by the hotel, enjoyed on the boat between Maya Bay and Pileh Lagoon
meals.dinner: Seafood BBQ dinner at a top Phi Phi restaurant — lobster, barramundi, and sticky rice mango dessert

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has strict visitor limits and timed entry — book through your hotel concierge well in advance. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the marine ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private longtail boat tour around Phi Phi Don's quieter northern bays — visit Laem Tong Beach and Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Phai) for pristine white sand and shallow snorkeling. These spots are far less crowded in the early hours. Enjoy a fresh coconut on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phi Phi Don and explore Tonsai Village on foot — browse local artisan shops and pick up handcrafted souvenirs. Visit the local fresh market for an authentic street food experience: try pad kra pao (basil stir-fry), mango sticky rice, and fresh-pressed sugarcane juice. Rest at the hotel pool during the hottest part of the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Thai cooking class hosted by a local chef — learn to prepare tom kha gai (coconut soup), pad thai, and mango sticky rice using fresh local ingredients. Enjoy your creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — smoothie bowls, pastries, and Thai herbal teas
meals.lunch: Street food tour through Tonsai Village market — multiple small dishes including grilled satay, fresh spring rolls, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Private Thai cooking class dinner — dishes you prepare yourself with a local chef

day_by_day.notes: The street food market is best explored before 14:00 when vendors begin packing up. Bring small cash denominations for market purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phi Phi Islands via private speedboat to Krabi Town (approximately 1.5 hours). Check in to a luxury property in Krabi such as Rayavadee Resort or Phulay Bay, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve. After settling in, take a private longtail boat to the iconic Four Islands tour — visiting Koh Mor, Koh Tub, Koh Chicken, and Poda Island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Railay Beach — accessible only by boat, this limestone-flanked paradise is one of Thailand's most dramatic coastal settings. Visit Phra Nang Cave Beach and the sacred princess cave shrine. Try stand-up paddleboarding or kayaking through the sea caves and hidden lagoons of Railay East.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town for an evening exploration of the famous Krabi Walking Street Night Market (open Thursday to Sunday) or the Maharaj Fresh Market. Sample authentic local street food including fresh oysters, grilled corn, and khao pad (fried rice). Enjoy a rooftop cocktail overlooking the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full Thai and Western spread with Andaman Sea views
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a Railay Beach restaurant — grilled fish, papaya salad, and cold Singha beer
meals.dinner: Krabi Night Market street food experience followed by craft cocktails at a rooftop bar

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach is only accessible by longtail boat from Ao Nang or Krabi Town — arrange through your hotel. If visiting on a non-market night, the Ao Nang beachfront has excellent dining alternatives.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day kayaking adventure through the mangrove forests of Ao Thalane — a UNESCO-recognized ecosystem. Paddle through narrow channels, spot wildlife including monitor lizards and exotic birds, and explore hidden sea caves accessible only at low tide. A private guide provides naturalist commentary throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Sua) — climb the famous 1,237 steps to the summit for extraordinary 360-degree views over Krabi Province. This is a significant spiritual site, so dress modestly. Return to the resort for a luxurious afternoon at the spa — try a traditional herbal compress massage.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset dinner cruise along the Krabi coastline — a chartered longtail or catamaran decorated with lanterns and fresh flowers. Enjoy a curated Thai fine-dining menu prepared by a private chef onboard, with champagne and wine pairings as the sun sets over the limestone karsts.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh tropical fruits, dim sum, and specialty Thai coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort pool restaurant — fresh salads, seafood wraps, and cold-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Private sunset dinner cruise — five-course Thai fine-dining menu with wine and champagne pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset dinner cruise at least 48 hours in advance through your hotel concierge. The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous — wear comfortable shoes and bring water.

day_by_day.morning: Private speedboat transfer from Krabi to Koh Lanta (approximately 1.5 hours). Check in to a luxury beachfront villa such as Pimalai Resort & Spa. Spend the morning on the pristine Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) — one of Koh Lanta's most beautiful stretches of white sand. Arrange a beach butler service through the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) — a charming, atmospheric settlement of century-old wooden Chinese-Portuguese shophouses built on stilts over the water. Browse independent boutiques, art galleries, and artisan craft shops. Visit the local Muslim fishing village for a glimpse into authentic island life.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at a cliffside beach bar overlooking the Andaman Sea. Dinner at one of Koh Lanta's acclaimed beachfront restaurants — try fresh-caught snapper in a tamarind glaze, massaman curry, and house-made coconut ice cream.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — tropical smoothies, eggs benedict with crab, and Thai congee
meals.lunch: Old Town café lunch — traditional Thai dishes in a heritage wooden shophouse setting
meals.dinner: Beachfront fine dining at Pimalai or a top-rated Koh Lanta restaurant — fresh Andaman seafood menu

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta Old Town is best explored on foot or by rented bicycle. The town is a protected heritage area — be respectful of local residents and property.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private island-hopping excursion by speedboat to the Koh Lanta Marine National Park islands — Koh Rok Nok and Koh Rok Nai. These are considered among the most pristine snorkeling and diving destinations in the Andaman Sea, with visibility often exceeding 20 meters. Snorkel over colorful hard coral gardens and encounter sea turtles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Koh Haa (Five Islands) — a cluster of dramatic limestone islands with an underwater cave system popular with divers. Non-divers can snorkel the exterior reefs. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch served on a private beach by your boat crew. Swim in the protected lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta for a beach bonfire evening arranged by the resort — complete with cocktails, live acoustic Thai music, and a BBQ dinner on the sand.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — energy-boosting options including açaí bowls, protein-rich Thai dishes, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on a private beach — charcuterie, fresh seafood, tropical fruits, and chilled wine
meals.dinner: Private beach bonfire BBQ — grilled lobster, tiger prawns, and local vegetables with Thai dipping sauces

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok and Koh Haa are within Koh Lanta Marine National Park — a national park fee applies. The journey to Koh Rok takes approximately 1.5 hours each way by speedboat.

day_by_day.morning: Morning wellness session at the resort spa — choose from a traditional Thai herbal steam bath, a detoxifying body wrap, or a holistic facial. Follow with a leisurely breakfast and a peaceful morning on the resort's private beach. Optional: join a guided meditation session offered by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer by speedboat from Koh Lanta to Phuket (approximately 2.5 hours via ferry and road, or arrange a direct speedboat). Check in to a luxury property such as Trisara, Amanpuri, or Rosewood Phuket. Explore the immediate surroundings of your resort.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Phuket Old Town for an evening street food walk — explore the historic Sino-Portuguese streets illuminated at night. Sample local Phuket specialties: mee hokkien (Hokkien noodles), o-tao (oyster cake), and khanom jeen (fermented rice noodles with curry). Finish with a premium cocktail at a heritage building bar.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread with made-to-order options and Andaman Sea views
meals.lunch: Light lunch onboard the transfer or at a stopover café
meals.dinner: Phuket Old Town street food walk — multiple small authentic local dishes and tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: Arrange your Koh Lanta to Phuket transfer through your hotel — options include speedboat to Ao Nang then road to Phuket, or a direct charter. Travel time varies by option chosen.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day tour of Phuket's Big Buddha (Phra Phutta Ming Mongkol Akenakiri) — an imposing 45-meter white marble statue atop Nakkerd Hill with sweeping views over the island. Continue to Wat Chalong, Phuket's most important Buddhist temple complex, for a guided spiritual and cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Phuket Old Town on foot — a UNESCO-recognized heritage district of beautifully preserved Sino-Portuguese architecture. Visit the Chinpracha House museum, browse the Saturday Walking Street (if applicable), and discover independent boutiques and galleries. Stop for an authentic Phuket-style afternoon tea at a heritage café.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar on Promthep Cape — one of Thailand's most celebrated sunset viewpoints. Dinner at a premium Phuket restaurant such as Suay, PRU (Phuket's only Michelin-starred restaurant), or a beachfront fine-dining venue in Surin or Bang Tao.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full luxury spread with freshly baked pastries, tropical fruits, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Heritage café lunch in Phuket Old Town — local Phuket dishes including mee sua and dim sum in a colonial setting
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred or premium fine-dining dinner — innovative Thai cuisine with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: PRU restaurant requires advance reservations — book at least one week ahead through your hotel concierge. Dress code applies at premium dinner venues.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private speedboat charter to the Similan Islands (approximately 1.5–2 hours from Phuket) — a national park archipelago consistently rated among the world's top ten dive and snorkel destinations. Snorkel the famous Elephant Head Rock and the shallow reefs of Island No. 4 (Miang Island). Encounter leopard sharks, rays, and turtles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Koh Bon or Koh Tachai (seasonal access) for more pristine snorkeling. Enjoy a gourmet lunch on the boat. Explore the jungle interior of one of the Similan islands on a short guided nature walk to the viewpoint for panoramic Andaman Sea vistas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phuket and unwind at the resort pool or beach. Enjoy a casual but premium dinner at the resort's signature restaurant, or venture to the Catch Beach Club at Bang Tao Beach for a glamorous evening of cocktails, fresh seafood, and live music.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — light and energizing ahead of a full day on the water
meals.lunch: Gourmet onboard lunch — sashimi, fresh salads, cold-pressed juices, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Beach club dinner at Catch Beach Club or resort restaurant — fresh seafood, cocktails, and ambient music

day_by_day.notes: The Similan Islands are only accessible from approximately November to April — October may be at the very start of the season. Confirm access with your operator. A national park fee applies.

day_by_day.morning: Indulgent morning at leisure — sleep in, enjoy a private pool villa breakfast, and use the resort's wellness facilities. Optional: book a private Muay Thai training session with a professional trainer at a premium Phuket gym for a unique cultural fitness experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Surin Beach and the upscale Millionaire's Mile — browse the luxury boutiques, galleries, and lifestyle stores in the Boat Lagoon or Porto de Phuket. Arrange a private longtail boat tour of Phang Nga Bay from Phuket — paddle through the iconic James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), sea caves, and floating fishing villages.
day_by_day.evening: Phang Nga Bay sunset — watch the sun descend behind the limestone karsts from your longtail boat. Return to Phuket for a premium dinner. Consider a traditional Thai khantoke dinner experience — a northern-style ceremonial feast served on a low lacquered table with traditional dance performances.

meals.breakfast: In-villa private breakfast — custom menu prepared by the resort's chef, served at your private pool
meals.lunch: Waterfront lunch at a top Phuket restaurant near the marina — fresh Thai cuisine and cold beverages
meals.dinner: Traditional Thai khantoke dinner experience or a premium beachfront restaurant in Surin

day_by_day.notes: The khantoke dinner is a cultural highlight — dress in smart-casual attire. Phang Nga Bay tours can be booked as a half-day afternoon excursion departing around 14:00.

day_by_day.morning: Final island-hopping adventure — private speedboat to Koh Yao Noi, a largely undeveloped island in Phang Nga Bay known for its authentic rural Thai lifestyle, rubber plantations, and stunning karst scenery. Cycle through rice paddies and fishing villages on rented bicycles with a local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkel the reefs around Koh Yao Noi and the nearby uninhabited islets. Enjoy a long, leisurely lunch at a local seafood restaurant overlooking the bay. Return to Phuket in the mid-afternoon and spend time at the resort beach or pool. Treat yourself to a final luxury spa treatment — a signature four-hand Thai massage.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Phuket's finest restaurants — consider Sala Phuket's beachfront dining, Acqua Restaurant (Italian-Thai fusion), or a private chef dinner arranged at your resort villa. Toast the journey with a bottle of champagne as the stars emerge over the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread, savored slowly on your final full morning
meals.lunch: Fresh local seafood lunch on Koh Yao Noi — whole grilled fish, green papaya salad, and cold coconut water
meals.dinner: Premium farewell dinner — multi-course tasting menu with wine or champagne pairing at a top Phuket restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Koh Yao Noi is a conservative Muslim community — dress modestly when cycling through villages. The island offers a beautiful contrast to the more developed parts of Phuket and Phi Phi.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning — enjoy a last Thai breakfast at the resort. Take a slow walk along the beach to collect your final memories of the Andaman Sea. Pack and prepare for departure. If time permits, visit a nearby local market for last-minute authentic Thai souvenirs: hand-painted ceramics, silk scarves, premium Thai tea, and artisan spices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort and arrange a premium private transfer to Phuket International Airport. Arrive with ample time for a comfortable departure. Browse the airport's duty-free for premium Thai products — OTOP-certified items, Thai silk, and gourmet Thai snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight — carry memories of 13 extraordinary days exploring Thailand's finest beaches, islands, and street food culture

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — indulge in your favorite dishes from the trip one last time
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or at a restaurant near the airport
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security at Phuket International Airport. Confirm your private transfer booking the evening before to ensure a smooth, stress-free departure.

query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026
